correctness.rationale: Finite-state absorbing-chain convergence is geometric at each fixed n. The exact exponential binomial moment reduces all parameter inequalities to scalar normalized-derivative comparisons; logarithmic derivative d-c/(1+cx) has the decisive signs at d=c and d=c/(1+c). Both normalized cumulative functions share endpoints, so strict interior inequalities follow. The truncated exponential CDF has gamma-derivative in [0,1], giving the stated exact bound beta^2/(n+beta). Multiplication conjugacy and known uniform one-step convergence yield both iterated limits. Finite code tests are supplementary only.

value.rationale: Long-iteration stability of a newly introduced approximation operator is a natural nonroutine question. The result replaces an (n-1)-unknown finite Markov absorption solve with two explicit strict closed-form barriers, gives an O(1/n) uniform quantitative theorem, and identifies a genuine noncommutation of approximation and iteration limits. It is not merely a restatement of one-step convergence or a generic diffusion heuristic.
